title: Any HN folks with undiagnosed diseases?
summary:
I've been suffering from a condition since around 2014 perhaps longer, that seemingly started after taking antibiotics (ciprofloxacin, Rocephin, Fosfomycin) where my body just loses tolerance to everything I continually ingest. What that looks like is something like an allergy, but my IgE testing on foods is all normal. For years doctors told me I was having panic attacks when I ate which seriously pissed me off. I started going to higher competence medical institutions and they did some testing during a reaction and low and behold one of the times they tested (for some reason only once...) the levels of PGD2 some allergy chemical were multiple times the upper limit of normal. So they thought maybe I have some kind of allergic disorder. They gave me steroids and antihistamines and it seemed to help. however, it only helped temporarily. Fast forward through me almost dying and being hospitalized with malnutrition repeatedly and spontaneously getting somewhat better years later, and I'm where I'm at now. I collect disability, but I suspect they're going to try to kick me off of it now that I'm doing somewhat better. The thing is, the reactions are totally unpredictable except just the knowledge that it will eventually happen with whatever I'm currently eating. It happens with medications too. So if they say "hey he's not taking his meds" what can I even say to that? I have reacted to numerous medications, including antihistamines and steroids.

Oh I didn't mention the symptoms with foods I react to: Just instant throat tightness/swelling, paleness, extreme bloating, nausea vomiting diarhhea, severe exertional intolerance in the hours following, cardiac arrhythmia, inability to swallow properly if it's bad enough, low blood pressure or high, just lasting for hours if I actually swallow the offending food. If I don't swallow it won't last as long. It's instantaneous as soon as it's in my mouth and I'm chewing on it it'll start. Like an IgE mediated allergy, except I don't swell up like a balloon externally, all internally.

Some specialist says I likely have MCAS but the testing for it is pretty hopeless, and SO MANY doctors flat out dismiss it as even a real thing. Just absolutely insane state of affairs.

But it's like, I just assume this is some bullshit because I've been basically poisoned by our current environment, and my microbiome destroyed by all these antibiotics for that infection in the past, and there's just no name for the condition. Cannon-fodder immune system destruction leading to loss of immune tolerance or something.

I've brought it all up with Claude 5.5 Opus and shit numerous times it's all useless. Just repeats back what I said basically. Tells me to see specialists I've already seen, etc. Nothing new at all. And if I'm not careful with my query, it'll just block me out too.

Anyone else like this? What do you even do in a situation like this?

title: Defect vs. Discrepancy vs. Missed Requirement
summary:
evening all. How does your team handle these situations where the AC is vague/does not specifically list out all of the requirements while the work meets the AC's as they are written but not as the product owner expected? My team has the habit of calling these defects & adding work to the original ticket. Also, when does a discrepancy count as a defect? For example a story AC lists "the work should match the approved mockups". So we could have all of the elements in place but maybe a 1px discrepancy in the spacing between two elements, or a component looks like the mockup until the dynamic behavior of the web-page is activated / data loaded/ action triggered etc.etc. How should these cases be handled? The acceptance criteria does not list the spacing between individual elements as a requirement nor the behavior of dynamic UI elements etc.etc.

title: "Decentralization" doesn't look decentralized
summary:
Billions in assets frozen within minutes, or at most a few hours.

So, what’s the difference between having a bank account where your funds can be frozen and holding blockchain tokens that can be frozen as well?

There are a few important conclusions:

1. Decentralization doesn’t mean ownership.

2. Decentralization of computational resources doesn’t mean decentralization of the assets you own.

3. Ownership isn’t yours (just partially) in either case: neither in TradFi nor in Crypto.

title: Xprtix – Browser-first media processing, vector editor, and 3D compressor (WASM)
summary:
I built XPRTIX (https://xprtix.com) because web tools shouldn't need to upload full media files to a remote server just to move a container header, shrink a video, or convert a HEIC photo.

XPRTIX runs these jobs directly in your browser. Files never leave your device.

Tools included in the suite: - Video: Fixes iOS video playback (relocates moov atoms and retags hev1 as hvc1 in-container without re-encoding), target-size compression (16MB WhatsApp, 10MB Discord, 25MB Email), format conversions, trimming, cropping, and MP3/GIF exports. - Image: Batch converts HEIC, WebP, AVIF, JPEG, and PNG. Handles resizing, cropping, compression, and EXIF location metadata stripping on save. - 3D: Inspects GLB, glTF, OBJ, STL, and PLY geometry, shows node weights, strips unseen geometry, and applies Draco or Meshopt compression locally. - SVG: Full-screen vector editor with node editing, boolean path operations, artboards, and clean React component code export.

Architecture: - Built with plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules (zero UI frameworks). - Uses native browser APIs and Mediabunny for fast local decoding. - Small WASM builds (FFmpeg, libheif, Draco, Meshopt) running inside Web Workers.

It is free to use, with no accounts and no watermarks: https://xprtix.com/

I'd value technical feedback on edge cases, broken files, or features you'd want added next.

summary:

I teach a youth group and have very little time to prepare lessons, but I can usually dump in an outline of a lesson and tell my AI to "make it clean and presentable" and it gives me polished slides that help engage the teenagers.

title: Ask HN: Agent swarm, orchestra, sequential, what's your workflow?
summary:
Hi, Something I've read here and there is people using LLMs for multi-agent orchestration, and I cannot fully understand the idea behind it. So for those of you who do, do you not review code anymore, as you're undoubtedly the bottleneck in this setup? How does this not end up in a chinese whisper game, especially considering how much LLMs infer, guess, and find edge cases and whatnot everywhere? I have two co worker, one is closer to my workflow, plans a lot, build one at a time, almost a duet with our company's LLM. Another one will take the conf room and voice mode over with his orchestrator, define all kind of things and full send it. One is a system engineer the other a web dev, but you get the idea.

I have looked at various attempt from people on github to implement these things, eg https://github.com/kunchenguid/firstmate; herdr itself; claude multi agent process. It has never worked out on my end, is it because of the complexity of the work or am I incompetent at delegating?

I understand the importance of mastering LLMs in this brave new world but to me it seems complicated to handle more than one at a time, especially if the problem is complex and requires reading/back and forth with it.

I'd appreciate resources of any kind to look deeper into it, or reading some of your work flows, good people of HN.

Cheers :)
